findings.evidence: specs/completion-lifecycle/spec.md:5 says "the review job, or finish without a queue, SHALL run a missing or stale review before finalize". The diff removes `ensure_review_evidence` from openspec_lifecycle.py. grep finds no production caller left; the only definition is template/scripts/independent_review.py:599. template/scripts/finish_task.py only calls `review_state` (observe, line 349) and `require_publication_review_evidence` (line 1082), and neither launches a review. The docs edit says "`finish` runs a missing, stale or unavailable review", which the code does not do. On a non-queue path a developer must run the review by hand, and the new archive error is the only prompt.
findings.summary: The modified requirement and the docs say that without a queue, `finish` runs a missing or stale review before finalize. The candidate removes archive's only review launch (`ensure_review_evidence`) and adds no replacement launch in `finish`.

findings.evidence: In openspec_lifecycle.py, `static_archive_problems` still does `raise SystemExit(f"Active OpenSpec change not found...")` before any collection. The managed-identity block collects only `ManagedTaskError`, and `source_issue_for_provenance` is called inside it. The spec says finalize "SHALL evaluate every archive precondition ... and SHALL fail once".
findings.summary: Finalize does not fully collect all preconditions into one failure. `static_archive_problems` still raises immediately when the change directory is missing, and unexpected failures in source-issue lookup are not collected. The existing refusal of managed candidates also exits early.
